issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require an addGuestStudents method with signature addGuestStudents(int, String) — i.e., it must accept an int and a String reason. The solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch between the specified API and the solution implementation can confuse students or graders about the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution's addGuestStudents method to match the specification: change its signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update the body to add the new guest students (e.g., this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents;). Optionally, record or log the reason parameter if needed. Ensure the template/tests and any documentation/UML consistently use the two-parameter signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a reason (String). The solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) (no String parameter). This mismatch in the method signature (missing reason parameter) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the task expect to implement or use a method with two parameters, but the provided solution only uses one.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement by changing the solution (and template) method signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason). If the reason is not used for logic, still accept the String parameter to match the specification (it can be stored, logged, or ignored with a comment). Ensure the constructor/comments and tests reference the two-parameter signature consistently.
